title: Backfill missing audit events and remediate KMS rotation race
creator: Aisha Patel
summary: Between 2026-03-01T02:17Z and 2026-03-01T03:03Z a subset of audit events emitted by the control-plane audit sink were not persisted to the long-term audit store due to a race during a scheduled KMS key rotation. Missing events include role grants, service account token exchanges, and 3rd-party SSO validation retries. This ticket tracks the backfill, remediation of the rotation race, monitoring/alerting improvements, and compliance sign-off.
timeline:
2026-03-01 02:15Z - Scheduled KMS rotation started.
2026-03-01 02:17Z - First dropped audit event detected by on-call when mismatch noticed in temporary buffer size.
2026-03-01 02:30Z - On-call escalated; rotation paused manually.
2026-03-01 02:45Z - Partial data recovered from ephemeral buffers; gap estimated ~45 minutes.
2026-03-01 04:00Z - Root cause initial triage identified as race between key swap acknowledgement and buffer flush path in audit-sink library.
2026-03-02 09:00Z - Incident declared security-sensitive; compliance and legal looped in.
2026-03-03 to 2026-03-10 - Backfill tooling prototype and patching work in progress.
investigation_notes: Root cause: audit-sink uses asynchronous encryption writer that assumes key availability is monotonic during flush. During rotation, the KMS client returned a new key id before the writer completed an in-flight flush; the writer dropped events if it could not successfully reinitialize within a 5s retry window. Secondary contributing factors: (1) rotation job did not emit an 'about-to-rotate' alert to the audit-sink, (2) no tail-scan replay job existed to detect contiguous gaps, (3) end-to-end tests never exercised live key rotations. Evidence: stack traces from audit-sink, KMS rotation job logs, Datadog span traces, and S3 object listings for the sink buffer.
action_items: Backfill: implement S3-based replay to insert missing events into long-term store and mark backfill run in compliance log (owner: Marco Liu, ETA 2026-03-18)
Fix rotation handshake: change rotation sequence to 'prepare->quiesce->swap->resume' and remove non-idempotent in-place reinit path (owner: runtime-team, PR required)
Increase audit-sink flush retry window to 60s and add jittered exponential backoff (owner: infra-team)
Add end-to-end CI test that performs a simulated KMS rotation while sending 10k audit events and asserts zero gaps (owner: qa, estimate 3)
Add Datadog alert 'audit.sink.gap_rate > 0 for 1m' with runbook to pause rotations and page security-on-call (owner: observability)
Tabletop with Compliance & Legal to validate backfill approach and archival integrity (owner: Security PM, scheduled 2026-03-12)
Perform full KMS key inventory and rotate any keys that used the old handshake library (owner: ops-team)
Publish detailed postmortem and remediation artifacts to Confluence and notify SOC and affected customers where required (owner: Aisha Patel)
Add audit log gap detection dashboard with per-customer and per-region granularity (owner: analytics)
Schedule a 6-week follow-up review to confirm no regressions after patch (owner: eng-managers, date 2026-04-30)
decisions: Do backfill rather than accept partial dataset: compliance requires full reconstruction or documented gap with approved backfill. Agreed 2026-03-02.
Hold live rotations until rotation-handshake patch merges and passes canary tests in staging (decision logged 2026-03-04)
Use S3 buffer replay as the canonical backfill source to preserve original timestamps and ordering (approved by Legal/Compliance)
Introduce a 'rotation-safe' library version tag; deployments must move to this tag before any rotation windows (adopted immediately)
notes: Compliance flagged this as a high-severity control gap. Legal has requested an auditable backfill run and attestations for the exact records replayed. We must preserve original event IDs and timestamps. Any modifications to events require an explicit 'replayed' flag in metadata. All backfill runs must be recorded in the compliance audit table.
